done.title: Fix shared blocker #2 and re-run the matrix
done.evidence: TM3: the second shared blocker was the missing SAHF/LAHF one-byte opcodes (0x9E/0x9F), not a JIT bug. The Halo repro (H:\Tests\XBOXReady\Halo ... v1.09) faults at exactly 604,260,882 steps, vec=6, EIP=0x00180AEC with --jit-raw, WITHOUT --jit-raw (IL), with --jit-exact and in accurate mode (604,264,734) - so every engine raises it. --break/--break-log show a single visit to 0x180AEC and --dumpv shows the byte is 0x9E = SAHF, the tail of the retail x87 loop fprem; fnstsw ax; sahf; jp (0x180AE6 FPREM -> 0x180AE9 FNSTSW AX -> 0x180AEC SAHF -> 0x180AED jp 0x180AE6); the decoder had no case for 0x9E/0x9F, so it raised #UD and the kernel's handler (EAX=0x1E exception number, ECX=0xC000001D STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, EBX/EDX = fault EIP) halted at 0x800151EF - the shared 'last EIP' in the matrix rows. Fix (xemu 0.8.139 target/i386/tcg/emit.c.inc gen_SAHF/gen_LAHF): Decoder 0x9E->Mnemonic.Sahf, 0x9F->Mnemonic.Lahf; XboxCpu Sahf = (Eflags & ~ConditionMask) | (AH & ConditionMask) with ConditionMask=CF|PF|AF|ZF|SF (0xD5, OF and every non-condition bit kept), Lahf = AH = (Eflags & ConditionMask) | Reserved1; SpecSahf/SpecLahf verbatim bodies + DecodedBlockCache.Terminates whitelist so the hot FPREM loop stays JIT-served. Evidence: FlagTransferTests (decode, six AH patterns, LAHF five-flag+bit-1 store, the sahf;jp FPREM branch both ways, round trip), JitTests.SahfLahfLoop (IL+raw vs interpreter, block served), SpecExecutionTests flag-transfer shapes - 15 tests, pre-fix build throws 'Unsupported instruction 0x9E'; tools/cpu-oracle gained 12 SAHF/LAHF cases and was regenerated against QEMU TCG (Unicorn 2.1.4), corpus 629 -> 641 all green (the reference confirms sahf_00 0xCD7->0xC02, sahf_d5 unchanged, lahf_8d5 AH=0xD7; a mask mutation fails the oracle). Titles: Halo 0xAC3AC fast / 0xAC543 accurate, Tak 0x39CE8B, Ninja Gaiden Black 0x37DC15 - 1B steps, LastFault vec=0. Matrix re-run (44 titles at 1B, serial): 2 own-render, 42 dashboard, 0 fault, 0 timeout (was 2/39/3/0); Tak is now the second own-render row (unique 2,675 draws / 41,995,882 px / 42 frames, EIP 0x39CE8B), Halo/NGB execute their own XBE code with no fault. done.evidence: 007 Agent Under Fire is playable: 100,000,000,000 steps with LastFault vec=0 (134,004 draws / 1,005,989,482 px / 6,478 frames, EIP 0x214C2), presenting the first-level Z8-on-the-docks scene (48,208 colours, 6.8% black, mean (78.7,65.5,45.3)); xemu 0.8.139 on the same ISO reaches the same scene at 150 s (63,994 colours, 6.8% black, mean (96.8,85.5,58.8); frame-compare --crop-top 0.25 dmean=(18.0,22.6,14.6), black 4.1% vs 4.2%). The 26.5B #PF (EIP 0x1C386E, CR2=0xE4) was our own duplicate SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE: McpxApuDevice.VoiceOff queued one on top of the VP frame walk (xemu voice_off sends none, mcpx_apu_vp_frame is the only sender), so the guest freed the voice on the first trap and dereferenced null on the second; the queue is gone and APU snapshot v5 keeps v2-v4 loadable. Scripted input from the 100B snapshot: 50M steps gives RAM 68E22299 (none) / 0FFAF650 (stick right) / 946C590A (stick left); at 300M the display is the plane-crash cinematic (13,754 colours) with no input or a held D-pad and black with a held A (cutscene skipped); across the boot the 20B no-pad frame is the Harrier intro and the A edge is what reaches gameplay. Save/load round-trips through the real EmulatorSession (72,110,280 B at 1.6B steps, faulted=False, tools/frontend-smoke) and the 100B snapshot resumes. Audio is a measured silence: --apu-dsp --audio-out writes 877,568 bytes / 219,392 frames of zero PCM (the VP mixer vp.c + AC97 are TM8). Gates byte-identical: accurate menu 4EF1FBF6/B6116DAE (5C0CF968/E2B4D327, 33,632/686/686), accurate triangle 5B50373D/79142DE4 (E58AE5D7/C43D5B49, 2,707/69/34), ktest CA5D3867 (40,797 B) at 792,800,535 steps; 44-row 1B matrix re-run unchanged (2 own-render / 42 dashboard / 0 fault / 0 timeout); suite 1988 -> 1990, build 0 warnings, format clean. Tooling: scripts/xemu-oracle.ps1 selects the disc through -config_path and captures a DPI-aware client area; tools/frontend-smoke falls back to data/xemu firmware.

rules.operator_order_2026_10_24: playable titles first: run the title matrix, fix the shared blockers in the current engine, and port an xemu module only when the matrix proves it blocks >=3 titles or >=20%; speed is reported, never claimed, until the playability gate is met
